answer: I fixed `slugify()` in `textkit/slug.py`. It now collapses each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a single dash and strips dashes from both ends, so `'Hello,  World!'` gives `'hello-world'`. `bb-test` passes (2 tests).

tool_calls.name: Edit
tool_calls.input: {"replace_all": false, "file_path": "<workspace>/textkit/slug.py", "old_string": "    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]\", \"-\", text)", "new_string": "    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", text).strip(\"-\")"}

diff:
--- a/textkit/slug.py
+++ b/textkit/slug.py
@@ -4,4 +4,4 @@
 def slugify(text):
     """Lowercase ASCII slug: runs of non-alphanumerics become one dash."""
     text = text.lower()
-    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
+    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text).strip("-")
